The cyclic HP-TES model showed excellent agreement in base heating capacity, system input power, and compressor inlet and outlet pressures throughout the TES recharge process, with slight deviations in compressor suction and discharge conditions during switching (see Figure 84). The deviations during switching are most likely due to refrigerant charge leaks that occur during recharging of the HP- TES, mainly when the system is manually controlled to allow the refrigerant charge to Page 86 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park escape from the indoor coil; this leaked charge is most likely in the low-pressure side of the cycle. When the cycle switches from recharge to base HP mode, the compressor discharge pressure and temperature increase suddenly, due to the lack of refrigerant charge in the indoor coil. This also results in the slow ramp-up of heating capacity in the indoor coil. Overall, the trends in system pressure, temperatures, and capacity are well captured. The two-operation HP-TES Modelica system-level model was able to seamlessly switch between modes, as intended. Consequently, a single complete model was developed, capable of operating in base HP, discharge, and recharge modes, with check valves that change the refrigerant flow direction depending on the operating mode. The cyclic HP-TES recharge-and-discharge model validation in cooling mode was implemented for Test 11C (ambient 95°F/75°F) (Figure 85). The order of operation was TES recharge followed by discharge, repeating every 15 minutes for 2 total hours. A potential reason for this degradation was the delay in refrigerant charge migration when switching between discharge and recharge, resulting in the discharge mode operating at a lower refrigerant charge. The HP-TES system models predicted discharge capacities similar to those in Test 3C but overpredicted the intermittent discharge cooling capacity. However, the TES discharge and recharge rates and power demand were well predicted (<2%). The model also predicted the refrigerant and water state points with minor deviations, capturing the overall transient behavior of the HP-TES.
